results.title: Creative data justice: a decolonial and indigenous ...
results.content: The decolonial framework is rooted in the indigenous systems of care (Silva et al., Citation2022) which entails: (1) reframing value systems by attending to a diversity of aesthetic standards and (geo)politics of creative value; (2) pluralizing evaluation criteria that values creative forms within their contextual milieu rather than relying on universalized and hierarchical frameworks; (3) promoting reciprocal knowledge exchanges between creative stakeholders from the Global North and South; (4) developing North–South networks to support the agency and solidarity among creators and institutions globally that are committed to democratic and fair creative value, and South–South networks for direct exchange without the mediation of the Global North; (5) prioritizing indigenous practices and narratives to sustain local cultures and resist homogenization, and build guardrails to prevent their creative value from being co-opted or commodified by global markets; (6) critical engagement with power dynamics by contextualizing creative works within their historical and contemporary geopolitical settings; (7) developing fair and equitable practices within the global creative economy that prioritize the interests of especially underrepresented creators from the Global South; and (8) moving beyond the neoliberal market-driven value by including alternative economic systems such as cooperative ownership of creative work, or community-supported art projects that reflect collective, rather than individual value.
